themes_detail.label: Police Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Real Time Enforcement complaints and Internal Affairs Division (IAD) complaints spiked dramatically THIS WEEK—6 RTE complaints and 3 IAD complaints vs. 0.6 and 0.2 weekly averages respectively—suggesting a possible pattern of resident dissatisfaction with NYPD operations or accountability in CD 302.
evidence: Real Time Enforcement complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.72)
IAD complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35)
Both complaints represent new complaint categories spiking simultaneously
reporting_angles: Investigate what specific enforcement actions or disciplinary decisions triggered the surge in complaints
Interview residents and community leaders about recent police interactions and accountability concerns

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped 130% THIS WEEK to 25 complaints vs. 10.9 weekly average, coinciding with a broader noise surge across residential and street categories, suggesting new commercial activity or event scheduling problems in the district.
evidence: Commercial noise complaints: 25 THIS WEEK vs. 10.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.39, up 130%)
Concurrent spike in overall Noise complaints: 71 last week vs. 30.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.3, up 132%)
Residential noise remains second-highest complaint type at 1,801 over 90 days
reporting_angles: Identify which businesses or venues in Fort Greene or Brooklyn Heights are generating new noise complaints
Check if any new restaurants, bars, or entertainment venues recently opened or expanded operations

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Flooding Streets
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints exploded 1500% LAST WEEK to 4 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average—the largest proportional spike in the dataset—indicating a possible CitiBike or other bike-share malfunction, theft pattern, or new dumping issue.
evidence: Abandoned bike complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66, up 1500%)
Largest z-score spike in dataset, indicating statistical anomaly
Complaint type rarely appears in baseline data
reporting_angles: Contact CitiBike and other bike-share operators to determine if there is a specific malfunction, rebalancing issue, or theft spike
Photograph and map where abandoned bikes are concentrated in Fort Greene or Brooklyn Heights

themes_detail.label: Building Use Code Violations Rising
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked 500% TWO WEEKS AGO to 6 complaints vs. 1.0 weekly average, suggesting potential illegal conversions, unpermitted occupancy changes, or zoning violations coinciding with active ULURP applications (395 Flatbush Ave, Columbia Heights rezoning).
evidence: Building/Use complaints: 6 two weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.0, up 500%)
1,180 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (855 Alterations), indicating active construction
395 Flatbush Avenue Ext. Redevelopment and Columbia Heights Rezoning currently in public review/filed stages
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint addresses with active ULURP applications and DOB alteration permits
Interview residents about illegal conversions or unpermitted occupancy changes near development sites

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Resurgence
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints spiked 500% THREE WEEKS AGO to 3 complaints vs. 0.5 weekly average, indicating a possible seasonal pattern or emerging open-air market issue, though signal is slightly older than other spikes.
evidence: Drug activity complaints: 3 three weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.0, up 500%)
Brooklyn Eagle article on homelessness in Downtown Brooklyn (2026-04-07) may indicate related quality-of-life concerns
Complaint type rarely appears in baseline data
reporting_angles: Identify specific locations where drug complaints are concentrated (parks, blocks, transit hubs)
Interview community board members and local precinct about enforcement response and root causes
